2022-50051.text:
## How they got there
Real Madrid secured the title by defeating Liverpool 1-0 in the final. Their path was defined by a profile of exceptional ball retention and discipline, featuring 670 passes per game where they performed better than 100% of teams, alongside a pre-season UEFA club coefficient of 127.0 points that beat 97% of peers. They also maintained superior control with only 7.8 fouls committed per game, outperforming 97% of the season's competitors in this metric.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Real Madrid for the final, as they ranked fifth among knockout teams and fell outside its top two preference threshold. Although the model assigned a 19.0% probability of reaching the final compared to a base rate of 12.5%, it estimated their expected stage as semi-finals rather than the winner's circle. The prediction was pushed upward most by attacks per game, which contributed 0.37 to the score, and fouls committed per game, contributing 0.3. Conversely, the model viewed long passes (% of passes) as a negative factor with a contribution of -0.08, followed by opponent shots on target per game at -0.05.

## Weak spots
Real Madrid's long passes accounted for only 8.8% of their total volume, a figure that beat just 6% of teams in the group phase and 6% historically. They covered an average distance of 110.3 km per game, performing better than only 12% of their peers in the same season and 29% over the long term. Additionally, they conceded 9.0 opponent shots per game, a defensive metric where they beat just 44% of teams during the group stage and 61% historically.

2022-7889.text:
## How they got there
Liverpool reached the final as runners-up after losing to Real Madrid 0-1. Their campaign was defined by a dominant profile, featuring a Points per game average of 3.0 that placed them better than 97% of teams in their group and league phase, alongside Shot accuracy at 59.2%, which beat 97% of peers. They also maintained high control with Possession at 59.5%, outperforming 97% of the season's teams on this metric.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Liverpool, ranking them second among all knockout teams and placing them inside its top two predictions. With a calculated probability of 31.7% to reach the final, the system viewed their chances as higher than the base rate of 12.5%. The nearest stage to the model's expectation of 2.23 was the semi-finals. This outlook was driven upward by Attacks per game with a value of 57.5 beating 84% of teams (SHAP contribution 0.44), while Pre-season UEFA club coefficient at 101.0 points, beating 75% of teams, pushed the prediction down most (SHAP contribution -0.07).

## Weak spots
Distance covered per game was recorded at 113.1 km, a figure that beat only 25% of teams in the group and league phase. Fouls committed per game stood at 12.0, which was better than just 38% of their seasonal peers despite being marked as lower is better. Long passes accounted for 13.1% of all passes, a metric that beat only 47% of teams in the group and league phase.

2025-50138.text:
## How they got there
Inter reached the final as runners-up after losing to Paris Saint-Germain with a score of 0-5. Their campaign was defined by exceptional efficiency, ranking in the top tier for Points per game at 2.38 where they were better than 94% of teams in the group phase. They also demonstrated elite defensive solidity, allowing just 2.9 opponent shots on target per game to be better than 89% of their peers, alongside a strong Goal difference per game of 1.25 that outperformed 88% of teams.

The model would not have selected Inter as a top-two finalist, ranking them ninth with a probability of 7.7%, which sits slightly below the base rate of 8.3%. Based on historical data from other seasons, the model's expected performance aligns nearest to the quarter-finals at an expectation level of 0.84. The prediction was pushed upward primarily by Long passes (% of passes) with a contribution of 0.14 and Shots per game contributing 0.08. Conversely, the outlook was dampened significantly by Attacks per game with a negative contribution of -0.16 and Shot accuracy (% on target) at -0.13.

## Weak spots

Finally, a Shot conversion rate of 13.9 meant they outperformed only 36% of teams in that metric during the group stage.

2025-52747.text:
## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain secured the title by defeating Inter 5-0 in the final. Their path was defined by a profile of high-volume attacking play, evidenced by 65.5 attacks per game where they performed better than 94% of teams in the league phase and 97% historically. This offensive output was supported by 13.2 shots per game, beating 97% of their peers that season, while maintaining a tight defense with just 6.0 opponent shots per game, a figure superior to 94% of teams both locally and across the competition's history.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Paris Saint-Germain as a primary finalist candidate, ranking them eighth against its top two choices despite their eventual victory. While the club achieved a 9.6% probability of reaching the final, this figure sits only slightly above the 8.3% base rate for a random knockout team. The model's expectation aligns closest with the quarter-finals stage rather than the ultimate prize. This assessment was driven upward by an SHAP contribution of 0.41 from 65.5 attacks per game and downward by -0.19 from 9.1 long passes (% of passes).

## Weak spots
Paris Saint-Germain's reliance on only 9.1 long passes as a share of total passes placed them better than just 17% of teams in the league phase. Their efficiency in finishing was limited, with a shot conversion rate of 13.2% that outperformed only 26% of their divisional rivals. Additionally, they achieved shot accuracy on target at 46.2%, a metric where they surpassed merely 33% of teams during the group and league phases.

2026-52280.text:
## How they got there
Arsenal reached the final as runners-up after losing to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties following a 1-1 draw. Their campaign was defined by an exceptional league profile, where they finished with 3.0 points per game and a goal difference of 2.38 per game, beating 100% of teams in the group phase for both metrics. They also limited opponents to just 2.8 shots on target per game, a defensive figure that placed them ahead of 97% of their peers during the league stage.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Arsenal as a top contender, ranking them second among all knockout teams with a 24.6% probability of reaching the final. This likelihood is higher than the 8.3% base rate for a random team to reach this stage, leading the algorithm to expect a semi-final exit rather than an early departure. The prediction was driven upward most by their goal difference per game of 2.38, which contributed 0.78 to the model's expected stage score. Conversely, the view was pulled downward primarily by their attacks per game value of 50.1, which carried a SHAP contribution of -0.16.

## Weak spots
Arsenal committed fouls at a rate of 13.9 per game, beating only 11% of teams in the league phase for this metric where lower is better. Their reliance on long passes accounted for just 11.4% of their total volume, a figure that placed them ahead of only 36% of peers. Additionally, they averaged 450 passes per game, a statistic where they outperformed merely 39% of the teams in the same season's group phase.

2026-52747.text:
## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain secured the title by defeating Arsenal on penalties in a final that ended 1-1, with a 4-3 penalty shootout deciding the winner. The club's profile is defined by an overwhelming dominance in ball control and creation, boasting 100% of teams beaten for Shots per game (14.9), Possession (64.1%), and Passes per game (671) during the group phase. These metrics place them among the top performers historically, beating 94% to 99% of all Champions League teams since 2011-12 in these categories.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Paris Saint-Germain as a primary pick, ranking them fourth among knockout teams despite their status as a leading contender outside its top two choices. While the base rate for any random team reaching the final is 8.3%, the model assigned this squad a 15.9% probability of success. The stage on the expected scale nearest to the model's expectation of 1.66 is the semi-finals, rather than the actual victory. This assessment was driven upward by Attacks per game (0.42) and Goal difference per game (0.2), while being pulled downward by Long passes (% of passes) (-0.19) and Shots per game (-0.1).

## Weak spots
Paris Saint-Germain beat only 8% of teams in that season's group phase for Long passes (% of passes), a figure representing just 5% historically since 2011-12. The team also ranked poorly relative to peers in Distance covered per game (km), beating only 28% of the season's teams and 62% of all historical Champions League participants.

synthesis.text:
## Why the best teams win

The model trained on 256 knockout team-seasons using group and league-phase stats achieved a mean within-season Spearman correlation of 0.45 with a 95% interval from 0.34 to 0.54, an AUC for reaching the final of 0.73 with an interval from 0.61 to 0.83, and a Brier score of 0.098 compared to a base-rate guess of 0.103. The resulting Brier skill was 0.05 with an interval from -0.04 to 0.13; because this interval includes zero, the edge over the base-rate guess is inconclusive on that measure. Meanwhile, 46.7% of actual finalists appeared in the model's top four, compared to a random ranking share of 23.9%; since the 95% interval for the model's share ranges from 30.0 to 60.0 and does not include the random value, the whole interval lies above it.

Deep runs are associated with stats where pedigree, results, or style matter most, though feature-set comparisons show overlapping intervals so differences between these categories are tentative. The top stat is Attacks per game from the style group with an importance of 0.229 knockout stages and a robustness label of robust. Goal difference per game follows as a results stat with an importance of 0.198 and a robust label, while Long passes (% of passes) is a conditional style stat with an importance of 0.135 that points the other way on its own. Passes per game is another robust style stat at 0.119, whereas Fouls committed per game is model-dependent at 0.094 and Shot conversion is conditional at 0.086.

## Winners vs runners-up

Across all finals, Pre-season UEFA club coefficient had a mean difference of 0.57 with a Holm-adjusted p of 0.111, while Fouls committed per game showed a mean difference of -1.13 and a p of 0.181. Shots per game recorded a mean difference of 0.79 with a p of 0.292, and Pass accuracy had a mean difference of 0.76 with a p of 0.422. None of these four differences reached the significance threshold of 0.05 for Holm-adjusted p-values.

In terms of frequency, the winner was higher in Pre-season UEFA club coefficient in 13 finals and lower in 2; for Fouls committed per game, the winner was higher in 2 and lower in 12 with one tie. Regarding Shots per game, the winner was higher in 11 finals and lower in 2 with two ties, while Pass accuracy saw the winner higher in 12 and lower in 3 with no ties. No difference among these four stats was significant because all Holm-adjusted p-values remained above the threshold.
